name: Redline
jobs: Slides, decision briefs, launch pages, posters

tokens.name: paper
tokens.usage: Page ground and the paper slide surface.

tokens.name: paper-raised
tokens.usage: Cards, fields, the paper stage inside an ink page.

tokens.name: paper-sunk
tokens.usage: Wells, tracks, table stripes, off dots.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairline rules: list rows, footers, the slide foot.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Type, rules, the ink slide surface, the ink half of the split bar.

tokens.name: red
tokens.usage: The one colour. The red slide surface, the primary button, the accent half of a bar, the on dots. Unchanged in Night.

tokens.name: on-red
tokens.usage: Type on red: ink, never paper, so red surfaces stay printed, not glowing.

tokens.name: red-ink
tokens.usage: Red as text on paper: one word in a headline, a link, a delta.

tokens.name: red-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for selected rows and red callouts; text on it is ink.

tokens.name: positive
tokens.usage: Up, done, approved. Always with a word or a glyph.

tokens.name: negative
tokens.usage: Down, failed, refused. The same red: errors are loud, there is one red.

type_roles.name: display-xl
type_roles.usage: The cover word. One per deck or page; it may run off the stage.

type_roles.name: display-m
type_roles.usage: Page titles, big labels beside a number.

type_roles.name: title
type_roles.usage: Card titles, list heads, feature titles.

type_roles.name: body-l
type_roles.sample: Customers return. But service takes time.
type_roles.usage: Decks and the one sentence under a number.

type_roles.name: body
type_roles.sample: The wait signals a service constraint; it does not establish demand for a second site.

type_roles.name: body-s
type_roles.sample: Source: supplied brief. Proposal, not an approved investment.

type_roles.name: label
type_roles.usage: Eyebrows, toplines, list numbers, stamp text. Mono caps through CSS.

type_roles.name: numeral
type_roles.usage: KPI figures and the giant slide number. Condensed, tabular.

idea_headline: A poster that makes a decision.
idea: Redline sets a brief the way a good poster does: one condensed word that fills the surface, one number big enough to read from the back of the room, one red. Three surfaces (paper, red, ink) give a deck its rhythm, and small printed devices (a dotmatrix, a stamp, a split bar, a stripe) carry the figures. Everything is flat ink on stock. Nothing glows.
use_for: Slide decks and decision briefs, launch and campaign pages, one-page proposals, posters, anything whose first screen must be read in a second and remembered.
avoid_when: Long reading (condensed caps tire past a paragraph), dashboards with many simultaneous numbers, subjects that need warmth, softness or more than one colour.
principles_headline: Five rules, printed in one colour.
principles: The cover word is set at .82 leading and may run past the edge. It is the whole slide; the sentence below it is small.
One number, big enough for the back row.
A slide carries one figure in the numeral role. Supporting figures go in the list rows at a tenth of the size.
Paper is the default, red is the moment, ink is the evidence. A deck changes surface no more than every third slide.
Dotmatrix for a share, split bar for a sum, list rows for a ranking, stamp for a status. No decorative shapes.
It is the surface, the accent and the error at once. Green and amber exist for status words, never as design.
voice: Short declaratives, present tense: "Customers return. Service takes time."
Say what a number is and what it is not: "An illustrative throughput, not a demand forecast."
Toplines name the deck and the slide: LOOP / 02.
No exclamation marks. The type is already shouting.
colour_headline: Paper, ink, red. That is the palette.
colour_note: Day first: paper ground, ink type, red for the surface that matters. Night is the ink slide as the page: ink ground, paper type, the red unchanged. Type on red is always ink, so red stays printed rather than lit. Status words use green and amber; the error colour is the red itself.
chart_note: Red is the series the slide is about; ink is the comparison; ink-soft the baseline. Prefer the split bar or the dotmatrix to a chart when the figure is one share or one sum.
type_headline: Barlow Condensed shouts, DM Sans explains, DM Mono files.
type_note: Barlow Condensed at 700, uppercase, tracked to -.025em and set with .82 leading for the cover word and .9 for titles. DM Sans carries every sentence. DM Mono carries toplines, list numbers and stamps at 11px with .09em tracking.
space_headline: Stage units on slides, a 4px base on pages.
space: Gap in a stamp, dot gap in a dotmatrix.
Between a title and its number.
Slide side padding, in container units so a slide scales.
Slide top padding; the foot sits 2.2cqw from the bottom.
edges: Everything. Buttons, fields, cards, stages, tags. A poster has no rounded corners.
Line-coloured hairlines on list rows, the foot and the topline.
currentColor, under a metric row or a slide section.
Stamps and outline buttons use a 2px currentColor border.
depth: No shadows, no elevation. Surfaces change colour instead of height.
A giant word at 20% opacity, rotated -12°, behind a decision slide. One per deck.
Grayscale, multiplied onto red at 88%. Never full colour.
motion: Buttons invert to ink, 200ms. Rows do not react.
3px outline in red on paper, in paper on ink; 5px offset.
A slide enters with a 12px slide-in and fade over 420ms; its headline rises 20px over 650ms (kit animate-fade-up).
Long pages reveal sections with reveal-up; the dotmatrix fills dot by dot with a 20ms stagger.
None. A marquee is allowed on a launch page only, once, for a list of names.
components_headline: The kit wears paper and red; the devices are classes.
components_note: Kit components take Redline through the contract: paper grounds, red primary, ink secondary, zero radius. The stage, the dotmatrix, the split bar, the stamp and the list row are authored rl-* classes written against the hand variables, so they port.
buttons: <Button>Approve the site</Button><Button variant="secondary">Request numbers</Button><Button variant="outline">Download brief</Button><Button variant="ghost">Later</Button><button className="rl-btn rl-btn-primary">Approve the site</button><button className="rl-btn rl-btn-ink">Request numbers</button><button className="rl-btn">Download brief</button>
buttons_note: Kit buttons on the left; authored rl-btn on the right: condensed caps, 2px edge, square, inverted on hover. One red button per surface. On a red surface the primary is ink.
tags: RedInkDraftRefusedLoop / 02Proposal▲ ApprovedWaiting▼ Refused
tags_note: Tags are mono caps in a 1px box. Status tags carry a glyph or a word with the colour; the red tag is a surface, not a status.
fields_note: Fields are paper-raised with a 1px line edge, square, with condensed caps labels above. Focus is a 3px red outline. The segmented control fills its active segment red with ink type.
stats:
Repairs / monthtoday, across one site
Added capacity+if the second site opens
Days waitingmedian, last quarter
stats_note: A stat is a mono label, a condensed numeral and one sentence, over a 2px rule. The red stat is the one the slide is about. Figures come from data.
callouts:
Proposal, not an approved investmentEvery figure is illustrative until finance signs.
Red means the moment. The one thing this slide asks you to decide.
▲ Approved. The second site opens in Q2.
▼ Refused. Demand is not established. Bring the waiting-list data.
callouts_note: A callout states the decision, then the condition. Status grounds are the soft tokens; the type stays ink.
chart_comp_note: Charts take red first, ink second, square marks, no grid beyond the baseline. Use a chart only when a device cannot carry the figure.
table_note: Tables are list rows: a mono number, a condensed name, a sentence, each on a 1px top rule. No zebra, no cell borders.
card:
Loop / 03 · The proposal

More room. Same mission.

240+160
Current repairs / monthAdded capacity / month

The second site adds capacity equal to two-thirds of today's volume. 400 a month is an illustrative throughput, not a demand forecast.
card_note: A card is a paper stage in miniature: topline, condensed title, one device, one sentence, one action. Flat, square, hairline-edged.
motifs_note: Redline draws with flat ink on stock: 2px square-capped strokes, flat red or ink fills, no shadow. Its own devices below; each carries a figure, none is decoration.

motifs.usage: A status lands as a mono stamp in a 2px box rotated -4°. Behind a decision slide, the decision word sits at 20% opacity, rotated -12°, as a watermark. One each per deck.

dos: One word per cover, set to fill the surface.
One number per slide, in the numeral role.
Change surface (paper, red, ink) no more than every third slide.
Carry figures in devices: dotmatrix, split bar, list rows.
Set type on red in ink.
donts: No second colour; status words use green and amber, nothing else does.
No rounded corners, no shadows, no gradients.
No full-colour photos: grayscale, multiplied onto red.
No two red elements on one surface.
binding_losses: The three surfaces (red and ink as full slides), the split bar, the dotmatrix, the stamp, the watermark and the stripe have no contract slot. They are carried as --ds-* properties and the rl-* classes; kit components follow paper, ink and red but not the surface rhythm.
footer: Day first, Night second. Fonts: Barlow Condensed 500/700/800 + italic 700, DM Sans 400/500/700, DM Mono 400/500, all Google-hosted.

data.tab_body: Evidence: three numbers from the brief, nothing projected.

hand.headline: Flat ink on stock.
hand.note: Redline draws like a one-colour screen print: a 2px square-capped ink line, flat red for the part that matters, flat ink for the rest, sunk paper for the quiet parts. No shadow, no texture, no gradient; the figure sits in the display face. The subject is the artifact's; the hand is this. The `rl-paper`, `rl-red`, `rl-ink` and `rl-on-*` classes set SVG fills only; they do not paint HTML slides. For HTML, use stage classes such as `rl-stage-red`, which set background and text colors.
rules: Flat red for the one thing; flat ink for the comparison; sunk paper for the rest.
None. Depth comes from the surface change, never from an offset.
DM Mono caps at 11px; Barlow Condensed for the one number.
A drawing may sit on paper, red or ink; on red its fills swap to ink.
A dotmatrix may fill dot by dot. Nothing else moves.

tpl.slide_sub: A second repair site: a proposal for more capacity, not a forecast of demand.
tpl.slide_body: Repairs a month, at capacity for the second month. Customers return; service takes time.
tpl.ed_deck: The workshop is full. The waiting list is eleven days long. Here is the case for a second site, and the one number it cannot prove.
tpl.ed_body: Two hundred and forty repairs a month is the ceiling of one room with four benches, and the room has been at it since August. The wait has climbed from six days to twelve. Thirty-eight of every hundred customers come back, which says the work is good; it does not say the work will grow. A second site adds a hundred and sixty a month of room. Whether it adds a hundred and sixty of demand is the question this brief leaves open.
steps: Each square is one repair. Red is finished inside the week; ink is waiting; sunk is referred elsewhere.
The rest wait a median of twelve days. The waiting is where the second site would act.
tpl.step_caption: Fig. 1 · One hundred repairs, by outcome · synthetic
tpl.landing_headline: More room for the next ride.
tpl.landing_sub: A second workshop in Q2, with a hundred and sixty more repairs a month. Same technicians, same mission, half the wait.
features: Twelve days today. Six when the second room opens.
The crew moves between sites; the standard does not.
Every price, every promise, printed in one colour so you can read it from the street.
